title: Renewal & Expansion: Flex slab pricing, uplift guardrails, and experimentation playbook
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Background: Enterprise customers frequently request flexibility at renewal to smooth over usage variance and to capture expansion upside. Current renewal mechanics (annual true-ups with flat multi-year discount) create friction: customers either over-commit to hit discounts or leave budget on the table. This ticket proposes a 'flex slab' renewal architecture (tiered committed bands + true-up cadence options) paired with explicit uplift/overage guardrails and a small set of controlled experiments to measure elasticity and churn impact. Work spans pricing design, contract language, sales enablement, legal sign-off, and an initial pilot with 6 enterprise accounts.
proposal_summary: Introduce a flex slab pricing model: 3 committed bands (Base, Growth, Enterprise) with optional annual or quarterly true-up cadence; add uplift rules that limit automatic escalation of discounts on sustained overages; provide a smoothing window (90 days) and a 'grace buffer' (10% of committed) before uplift applies. Offer multi-year buy-down discounts that increase with term length but taper for very large overages. Pilot with a subset of renewals and measure NRR, churn, and average contract value (ACV) changes.
pricing_model_details: Committed bands: Base (0-1M tokens/mo), Growth (1-10M), Enterprise (10M+). Each band has a specified unit price and an overage multiplier.
True-up cadence options: annual (default, lower admin), quarterly (optional, higher price), monthly (for high-velocity customers at premium).
Grace rules: first 90 days after renewal allow 10% over committed capacity without uplift. After that, uplift applies on sustained overage (>30 days above buffer).
Multi-year discounts: 1yr=0% baseline, 2yr=7% on committed spend, 3yr=12% with cap that discount does not apply to uplift/overage portion.
Smoothing: allow customers to spread catch-up true-up across remaining term in equal installments for contracts > $50k ARR.
Uplift guardrail: uplift is calculated on monthly sustained overage and capped at 50% of the committed band's unit price per month to avoid runaway discounts for sales-initiated expansions.
Audit & reporting: add explicit line items on invoices for committed spend vs uplift vs overage to improve transparency.
experiment_design: Cohorts: 1) Control renewal mechanics (current annual true-up, fixed discount tiers). 2) Flex slab with annual true-up. 3) Flex slab + quarterly true-up option + smoothing. Pilot target: 6 enterprise accounts per cohort (~18 total).
Primary metrics: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) at 12 months, ACV growth at renewal, renewal rate, time-to-sign, legal negotiation time.
Secondary metrics: Number of contract amendments, finance collections latency, support ticket volume during first 90 days post-renewal.

Success criteria: 1) +3% NRR lift vs control OR 2) reduction in negotiation time by 20% while maintaining <1% increase in customer disputes. Any severe negative (renewal win rate drop >5% or churn increase >2%) fails the experiment.
Duration & sample size: 12-month observation window with interim checkpoints at 90 and 180 days. Initial pilot duration 6 months focused on adoption and operational friction.
Randomization & rollout: Account selection stratified by ARR band and industry; opt-in for customers flagged as 'strategic' only after Sales approval.
contract_language_snippets: 'Committed Capacity' clause: Customer commits to a monthly committed capacity expressed in token units. Overages beyond the 'Grace Buffer' are subject to uplift as specified in Schedule A.
'True-Up & Settlement' clause: Customer may elect Annual or Quarterly true-up. Quarterly true-up includes a 3% premium to the committed unit price to offset operational cadence.

'Grace & Smoothing' clause: For the first 90 days post-renewal, up to 10% overage is considered part of committed capacity. For sustained overages, Customer may amortize the true-up over remaining term if contract value > $50k ARR.
'Uplift Cap' clause: Uplift applied to sustained overages is capped at 50% of the committed unit price per month; uplift is not eligible for additional multi-year discounting.
sales_playbook_steps: Step 0: Qualification – Sales flags renewal account for pilot; obtain written opt-in for flex slab pilot. Link to opt-in template in Drive.
Step 1: Offer – Present flex slab tiers with clear examples of invoice line items and smoothing option. Use 'savings vs over-commit' calculator (sheet link in artifacts).
Step 2: Negotiation – Standard redlines in clause library; limit custom uplift changes to Exec Sponsor approval only.
Step 3: Implementation – AM configures route in billing system to track committed vs usage; set 90-day grace window in telemetry.
Step 4: Monitoring – Weekly dashboard for pilot accounts (NRR, usage delta, disputes). Trigger immediate Product/Finance sync if support tickets >5 in a week.
Step 5: Post-renewal review – 90-day adoption check and 180-day commercial review; collect customer feedback surveys.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing rules implemented in billing system for committed bands, grace buffer, and uplift cap.
Contract clause templates added to clause library and signed off by Legal.
Pilot launched with at least 12 enterprise accounts enrolled and Sales/CS trained on playbook.
Dashboards showing committed vs usage by account and automated alerts for sustained overages.
Experiment tracking configured in Amplitude/Looker for primary metrics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers view uplift as punitive and push for deeper discounts. Mitigation: Clear examples and savings calculator; grace buffer; salesperson scripts emphasizing smoothing and flexibility.
Risk: Finance complexity increases for invoicing and revenue recognition. Mitigation: Finance and Engineering alignment upstream, billing templates, and automated line-item tagging.
Risk: Legal pushback on 'smoothing' or 'grace' contractual language. Mitigation: Provide fallback clause language and limit smoothing to contracts > $50k ARR.
Risk: Security questionnaire updates required for new billing telemetry. Mitigation: Coordinate with Security to append necessary controls and include equivalent answers in FAQ.
